note: Game data of the culture and faith layer (tools/content/modules/cultures.mjs). Names, tiers, languages, faiths and palettes come from world/cultures.json and country assignments from world/country_cultures.json; this file holds what the game adds: spirits, modifiers, hooks, text and the mappings other modules read. Every value is a proposed design target that can be tuned here. Modifier keys are checked against the installed game; values are checked against `bounds`.

lake_aenoran.spirit_desc: No lord may wage war for his own quarrel, and written law binds every house. Scribes, bells and barges keep the Lake's realms learned and slow to anger.
lake_aenoran.text: Farmers, bargemen and scribes of the Great Lake, the best-fed folk of Erdae. They keep written law and ring a bell for every order.

selen_ranger.spirit_desc: No bow is drawn in the Hallow Month, and no ranger shoots from rank. The woods are known, and the rangers wait in them.
selen_ranger.text: Rangers of the Selen woods, ruled by moots. They ask the wood before they loose an arrow.

steppe_rider.spirit_desc: A dispute is paid in mares, and a rider's herd feeds his host. Riders go far and build little.
steppe_rider.text: Horse-lords of Konori and Hunhun. Their land belongs to the herds, and their word to the horse they swear on.

wall_folk.spirit_desc: A post passes to the eldest of a watch-family, and a breach of watch is a hanging matter. The Wall is held with patience and drill.
wall_folk.text: Watch-families of the Great Wall. They keep its gates in the king's name.

march_folk.spirit_desc: Free farmers raise a levy at the beacon's call. Every farm is a post, and every beacon buys a day.
march_folk.text: Free farmers of the southern marches, led by elected speakers. They plough with a sling at the belt.

isle_houses.spirit_desc: The eldest woman of each house speaks for it, and daughters inherit. The island houses learn the sea early and watch it long.
isle_houses.text: Seafaring houses of Asgard, led by their eldest women. They know the central sea as a neighbour.

veiled_folk.spirit_desc: Debts and feuds are tied and untied on the cord, and strangers are not welcome. No charter has ever been read here.
veiled_folk.text: A veiled people of the Cursed Lands. They trade little and forgive nothing.

redbark_tribes.spirit_desc: Clans choose a war-chief for each raid and fight light and fast. They take iron where they find it and refuse every charter.
redbark_tribes.text: Clans of the Bloody Forest, led by cord-mothers. They paint themselves red and bow to no crown.

leren_sea_kings.spirit_desc: Shipowners vote the taxes, and the strait pays its tolls. The Leren read the sea as a ledger.
leren_sea_kings.text: Sea-lords of the Narrow Strait. One High Crown rules two realms, and a Speakers' Hall counts the ships.

free_crowns_north.spirit_desc: Neighbouring kings marry across their borders and take their feuds to Eekedor. Wars start slowly, and levies stay small.
free_crowns_north.text: Small kingdoms of the inland North, each ruled by a king with a council of landowners.

dondor_brutes.spirit_desc: A death is paid for in iron or in blood. Axe-men fight in mail behind shield walls and trust no spell.
dondor_brutes.text: Clan-moot kings and iron-halls of Dondor. They tax the iron road and leave magic to the Fire-speakers.

mirolon_wardens.spirit_desc: Every tower keeps a lamp lit toward the south, and every warden keeps a night watch. Scouts and couriers see a host long before it comes.
mirolon_wardens.text: Wardens of the lake and the northern passes, chosen for life by their captains.

dead_lands_freeholds.spirit_desc: Freeholders bury quickly, tax lightly and avoid war. The sun and the salt have made them hard.
dead_lands_freeholds.text: Salt-pan and fishing freeholds of the Dead Lands coast. They do not speak of what lies to the south.

winter_crown.spirit_desc: No feud may be carried past a shared fire. The Long Dark is met by clans bound together.
winter_crown.text: The Winter Crown of the Cold Lands and its clan-fire keepers. They count the year in dark and light.

ice_clans.spirit_desc: Feuds are settled before the Long Dark begins. The clans move fast on ice and live hard on little.
ice_clans.text: Reindeer clans and sled-bands of the Cold Lands, ruled by chieftains of the moot.

isengard_warlords.spirit_desc: The best sworn man inherits the hall, not the eldest son. Mailed foot hold the mountain forts.
isengard_warlords.text: Warlords of the iron forts, bound by oath-companies. They suspect every hedge-wise.

windwaith_seafarers.spirit_desc: Land is held by share in a ship, and a Council of Captains elects its Speaker. Windwaith ships range far for timber and whalebone.
windwaith_seafarers.text: Captains of the Windwaith headlands. They read the wind the way others read letters.

gunwaith_clans.spirit_desc: Oaths are sworn at the stone and remembered by the Lawspeaker. Clan bands ride and fight for kin and for wergild.
gunwaith_clans.text: Hill clans of Gunwaith, whose kings are acclaimed at a standing stone. The chiefs hold the real power.

girdon_wardens.spirit_desc: Ford-wardens judge the river towns and keep every bridge in repair. A river militia digs in fast on its own bank.
girdon_wardens.text: Ford-wardens and bridge-towns of the Girdon rivers.

western_guilds.spirit_desc: Contracts are sworn on the guild book and enforced by the guild council. The towns hire their wars and pay for their workshops.
western_guilds.text: Guild towns of the western coast. They trade across the central sea and hire others to fight.

buldor_companies.spirit_desc: A company is its banner and its contract. Veterans drill quickly and cost much to keep.
buldor_companies.text: Hired companies of Buldor, who recruit from every clan. A fallen banner ends a company.

chart_islanders.spirit_desc: To chart a reef is a gift to every sailor to come. The chart-houses trade pearls and knowledge.
chart_islanders.text: Pilots and chart-houses of Triton's Islands. They sell their charts and keep their reefs.

corsair_lords.spirit_desc: A captive is ransomed or lost to the sea. Corsair lords take what they can and sell it back.
corsair_lords.text: Sword-lords of the cliff harbours. The isle's best captain wears its crown.

noris_riders.spirit_desc: Water is never refused, and one who seals a well is cast out. Camel-riders cross the sand where armies thirst.
noris_riders.text: Camel warriors of the Noris desert, led by the well-lords. They count their seasons by caravans.

caravan_princes.spirit_desc: A bench of merchant houses chooses the Prince and keeps the purse. Contracts are sealed, and hired companies fight them.
caravan_princes.text: Merchant houses of Stabilo who rule the caravan roads. Their law is contract and their weights are honest.

river_kings.spirit_desc: Temple scribes record the flood and the king's decrees. The river lends grain, and the temples lend their wizards.
river_kings.text: Kings of the river lands, named for their rivers and advised by temple scribes.

lake_road_cities.spirit_desc: Fishers and merchants share the water and the law. The lake towns grow with every caravan.
lake_road_cities.text: Lake towns on the road from the East to the Great Wall. They have kings in Ostoroth and speakers in Mora.

red_lands_tribunes.spirit_desc: A tribune holds office for one year and swears his oath again. The kilns never cool.
red_lands_tribunes.text: Clay-working villages of the Red Lands, led by tribunes chosen by the village heads.

southern_islanders.spirit_desc: Each harbour shares its catch at the feast, and its elder's word ends a dispute. War is rare and soon over.
southern_islanders.text: Reef and lagoon islanders of the south. They count their dead as waves on the reef.

zilin_pilgrims.spirit_desc: No weapon passes the hostel gate, and every traveller finds a bed and a lamp. The pilgrim valleys heal what the roads break.
zilin_pilgrims.text: Keepers of the pilgrim hostels in the Zilin Hills. They copy books, make salves and welcome all.

goodin_sunfolk.spirit_desc: Guest-towns shelter every pilgrim, and their elders settle disputes by agreement. The Sunfolk do not march to war.
goodin_sunfolk.text: Farmers of the sunlit guest-towns who live among the Sunhot elves.

forest_council_elves.spirit_desc: The houses vote, the First Speaker serves for centuries, and the book of precedents is renewed each hundred years. The council is slow, learned and gentle.
forest_council_elves.text: The great elven houses of the Magical Forest. They hold no crown and keep a book of precedents.

hill_kingdom_elves.spirit_desc: A hall's book of judgments is read aloud each spring. Hill rangers walk the ledges and read the signs of dragons.
hill_kingdom_elves.text: Elves of the hill halls, ruled by queens and kings whom the hall-keepers accept. They know dragon-craft best.

lake_elves.spirit_desc: A court of the water-houses judges disputes about weirs and boats. Dowsers and healers keep the lake-fevers away.
lake_elves.text: Boat-archers and healers of the elven lakes, led by the Speaker of the water-houses.

pass_wardens.spirit_desc: Each fort keeps a roll of its watch-houses, and a pass stays closed until the warden's vigil breaks. Little passes, and little is sold.
pass_wardens.text: Mountain archers and ropemen who have held the Nolorim passes for centuries.

rift_coast_elves.spirit_desc: Light-singers on the towers signal any crossing of the rift. Lantern, dye and salt cross the water to the river kings.
rift_coast_elves.text: Sea-archers and lantern-keepers of the Rift coast, led by the wardens of each shore.

gala_court.spirit_desc: The king reigns as long as he wills, and the keepers' rolls hold his law. Gala remembers Dardan and does not forget.
gala_court.text: The ageless court of Gala under King Lorien. They keep their dead in memory and their counsel quiet.

sunhot_light.spirit_desc: The tall guards stand in doorways and do not march. Warmth heals, and light turns the stranger aside.
sunhot_light.text: Sunhot elves of the Lands of Light, led by a Radiant Speaker whom the sanctuaries choose.

sunhot_western.spirit_desc: No weapon passes a sanctuary door, and every pilgrim road is kept open. The realms argue at the Council and seldom fight.
sunhot_western.text: Sunhot realms of the western sanctuaries, each led by a Speaker its sanctuary chooses.

sunhot_isles.spirit_desc: Quarrelling isles send their quarrel to the Lands of Light. Sea-law and sanctuary-law keep the harbours at peace.
sunhot_isles.text: Sunhot elves of the eastern isles, who sit at the Council of the Chain.

volcano_clans.spirit_desc: A warking holds the throne until a stronger orc breaks him in the ring. Hooked axes and war-beasts follow whoever wins.
volcano_clans.text: Orc clans of the fire-mountain, led by a warking whom the chiefs acclaim.

iron_clans.spirit: The Free Moot of the Holds
iron_clans.spirit_desc: Each hold keeps its iron and sends its chief to the moot to settle tolls and prices. Mail and chain go out by the bar.
iron_clans.text: Orc holds of the iron hills. A shared battle-horn calls their levies.

wild_holds.spirit_desc: A hold has a chief by strength and splits when it grows too big. Raiders trust charms and sell nothing.
wild_holds.text: Orc holds of the wild hills, with no council and no priest.

sea_orcs.spirit_desc: A sea-chief rules by voyages won, and captains meet in council on the Lestern Isles. Boarders with hooks take ships whole.
sea_orcs.text: Orc boarders of the skerries and the cliff harbours.

goblin_warrens.spirit_desc: The loudest, cleverest goblin leads until someone cleverer arrives. Traps, slings and tunnels do the fighting.
goblin_warrens.text: Tunnel-dwelling goblins under the orc holds. They sell lamps and traps to those above.
goblin_warrens.unused: No country has the warrens as its dominant or second culture: goblins are a minor people inside orc holds (demography.json, minor_peoples). The culture is kept for the state function (state_cultures.json) and for a future country.

troll_tribes.spirit_desc: The oldest troll who has not been beaten leads, and the loser feeds the tribe. They throw stones and fear fire.
troll_tribes.text: Bog-dwelling trolls of the Troll Forest, who heap stones at their borders.

hill_giants.spirit_desc: A dispute is judged by which side can name the older cairn. Giants quarry stone and raise walls that outlast kings.
hill_giants.text: Giants of Hiloron who count years by stones, led by a High Chief of the cairn-keepers.

ice_giants.spirit_desc: A Frost-King sits an ice throne chosen by the cairn-keepers. The cold itself is an old and patient ally.
ice_giants.text: Giants of Titanos who carve ice and ivory. They honour the cold as an elder spirit.

yeti_clans.spirit_desc: The clan follows the Eldest whose song carries furthest. Yeti hold the mountain at dusk and raid in winter.
yeti_clans.text: Furred clans of the Yeti Lands. Their names are sung at the winter gathering.

kilinti_ents.spirit_desc: The Eldest speaks last, and a moot may take three years to say one sentence. The forest is slow to rouse and nearly impossible to break.
kilinti_ents.text: The ents of Kilinti Forest. A few men live at its edge and keep its accounts.

grave_hosts.spirit_desc: The hosts march to the drum and answer to Volgan. They count their dead by name and do not leave the field.
grave_hosts.text: The dead and the living of Volgan's Dominion, led by his chosen captains. Mass hosts follow the dirge-drum.

zols_dead.spirit_desc: Numbered hosts march where Zol wills, and ordinary weapons do not end them. They build nothing and learn nothing.
zols_dead.text: The numbered hosts of Zol's Mistake. No tongue is recorded for them, and no rite.

netherborn.spirit_desc: Each lord keeps a pact and a pact-name, and oaths are sealed in blood and ash. The Netherborn are few and fearless.
netherborn.text: The demon realms of the Nether, each ruled by a Lord or Queen bound to a pact.

deliverer.spirit_desc: Believers keep a lamp and a loaf for the stranger and give a tenth of the first harvest to the Houses of the First Light. The Houses are clinic, granary and school.
deliverer.text: A New God of deliverance, protection and renewal, honoured in the Houses of the First Light. Its confessors teach and heal.

lamp_furrow.spirit_desc: Households honour the gods in two images, a lamp that never goes out and rain over a ploughed field. The mother keeps the lamp and the village keeps the rain-stone.
lamp_furrow.text: The folk faith of most households in the Middle Lands and beyond. It has no priests.

green_lords.spirit_desc: Every old wood has a Lord of the Green who must be asked before an arrow is loosed. No bow is drawn in the Hallow Month.
green_lords.text: A faith of woods and rangers, led by tree-wardens whom the moot chooses.

horse_oath.spirit_desc: A rider swears on a horse, and the horse carries the oath to the sky. An oath broken is a horse lost.
horse_oath.text: The faith of the steppe riders, witnessed by old riders called oath-riders.

stone_vigil.spirit_desc: The Wall is a promise to the dead of the Third Age, and every post is holy. Watch-chaplains keep the roll of the fallen.
stone_vigil.text: A faith of duty on the Great Wall and the marches.

isle_tide.spirit_desc: The dead go out with the tide and return with it. Each house names its ancestors in the tide-chamber at the flood.
isle_tide.text: The ancestor-faith of Asgard, kept by the tide-mothers.

old_knots.spirit_desc: Names are tied into a cord, and the dead are never untied. A stolen name is a cut cord.
old_knots.text: The oldest faith of the Orran folk, kept by cord-mothers.

strait_litany.spirit_desc: A litany is sung at every tide, naming the ships lost that year. The Leren sing to the gods and to the storm that took them.
strait_litany.text: The sea-faith of the Narrow Strait, with a litany-singer in each fleet.

winter_hearth.spirit_desc: In the Long Dark each house lets its fire go out and relights it from the clan fire. No family is alone with its cold.
winter_hearth.text: The ancestor-faith of the cold north, kept by fire-keepers.

storm_court.spirit_desc: Storms are the court of the sea. Captains and warlords bargain with the spirits of wind and water.
storm_court.text: A faith of wind-readers and storm-speakers.

clan_stones.spirit_desc: An oath sworn at a standing stone binds the stone, the swearer and the clan. The Lawspeaker remembers every oath.
clan_stones.text: The law-faith of the western hills, spoken by lawspeakers who are judges and priests together.

river_wardens.spirit_desc: Each river has a keeper that mistakes the town for a guest. The wardens feed it a loaf at the flood and keep the ford clear.
river_wardens.text: A faith of ford-wardens, who are also magistrates.

guild_hall.spirit_desc: Each guild honours one god under a craft-aspect and keeps a patron-day and a hall. Contracts are sworn on the guild book.
guild_hall.text: A faith of crafts, kept in the great halls of Kradlon and Corogon.

company_banner.spirit_desc: A company's banner is its soul, and sworn men pray before it. A fallen banner ends the company.
company_banner.text: The soldiers' faith of Buldor, led by banner-chaplains.

tide_charts.spirit_desc: To chart a reef is a gift to every sailor to come. A chart-house honours its first pilot and the reefs that spared him.
tide_charts.text: The pilots' faith of Triton's Islands.

ransom_tide.spirit_desc: The tide returns every ship. A captive who is ransomed is under the god of the harbour, and one who is not is under the sea.
ransom_tide.text: The law-faith of the corsair isles, kept by tide-judges.

well_oath.spirit_desc: A well is a promise from the earth. Sharing water makes kin, and one who poisons a well is cast from every tribe.
well_oath.text: The desert law-faith of Noris, kept by well-lords and well-wives.

scale_creed.spirit_desc: An honest weight pleases the gods. A false weight is the worst crime, and every temple keeps its scales.
scale_creed.text: The trade-faith of Stabilo, kept by weighers who also judge contracts.

river_temples.spirit_desc: The river is the oldest god we can see. Tall temples honour the gods above the flood-line, and the river below it.
river_temples.text: The faith of the river kings, served by temple scribes and flood-priests.

lake_litany.spirit_desc: The lakes keep the memory of the caravans. Merchants and fishers pray together at the water.
lake_litany.text: The lake-shrine faith of the Lake Road cities, read by lake-readers.

red_hearth.spirit_desc: The red clay is the bone of the first mothers. Each house re-fires its clay mother every spring.
red_hearth.text: The clay-faith of the Red Lands, kept by kiln-mothers.

wave_tally.spirit_desc: Each island counts its dead as waves on the reef. A shrine repeats a name long forgotten, and the islanders say the name is needed.
wave_tally.text: The ancestor-faith of the southern reefs, kept by tally-keepers.

noon_pilgrimage.spirit_desc: The Lands of the Sun are the nearest place to the divine realm that mortals call Heaven. The sanctuaries give rest to every pilgrim.
noon_pilgrimage.text: The faith of the Sunhot sanctuaries, kept by sanctuary-wardens and Keepers of the Noon.

kindred_song.spirit_desc: The elves hold that the world was sung and that to listen well is a duty. No elf claims to know the one true telling.
kindred_song.text: The reverence of the elves, kept by loremasters and song-wardens.

rain_mirror.spirit_desc: The Gala keep a spring where the past and the possible may be glimpsed. They do not trust a vision shown too plainly.
rain_mirror.text: The vigil of Gala, kept by the keepers of the Mirror.

festivals.name: The Reading of the Dead of Dardan

skull_fire.spirit_desc: The clan honours its dead on a cairn of skulls and its mountain with a fire that never goes out. Orcs do not say what lives in the mountain.
skull_fire.text: The ancestor-faith of the orc clans, led by Fire-Speakers.

hold_luck.spirit_desc: The holds trust charms, bones and lucky stones, and honour the spirit of whatever place they live in. Every priest is suspect.
hold_luck.text: The luck-faith of the wild holds, kept by charm-wives.

tide_skull.spirit_desc: Sea orcs sink a skull in the first catch of each season and pay the sea a tithe of salt.
tide_skull.text: The sea-faith of the orc skerries, kept by salt-priests.

warren_luck.spirit_desc: A warren trusts the luck of its lamp. A lamp gone out is a warren doomed.
warren_luck.text: The lamp-faith of the goblin warrens. The loudest goblin keeps the lamp.

stone_hunger.spirit_desc: The trolls honour the stone that feeds them and the hunger that drives them. Their dead are laid in bogs.
stone_hunger.text: The faith of the troll tribes. It has no priests.

giant_cairn.spirit_desc: A giant leaves one stone for each year of life. The great cairns are the giants' memory.
giant_cairn.text: The cairn-faith of Hiloron and Titanos, kept by stone-keepers.

yeti_hum.spirit_desc: The mountain hums, and the hum must be answered at dusk. A clan with no hum is lost.
yeti_hum.text: The faith of the yeti, kept by hum-keepers in the caves.

ent_slow.spirit_desc: The ents answer to the grove and the grove to the season. Men see no rite, and a moot may take three years to say one sentence.
ent_slow.text: The faith of Kilinti, which has no priests. The Eldest speaks last.

grave_cult.spirit_desc: The hosts keep a rite of Names and Gates, and many worship Volgan as a god.
grave_cult.text: The dark rite of the Dominion, kept by necromantic orders and the wardens of the Gates.

pact_rite.spirit_desc: Every lord keeps a pact and a pact-name known only to the pact. Oaths are sealed in blood and ash.
pact_rite.text: The dark rite of the Nether, kept by pact-heralds.

mourning_dust.spirit_desc: The dead are buried quickly and deep, with salt, and nothing is said of Zol or Volgan at the grave. Their gods are the gods of safe harbours.
mourning_dust.text: The mourning customs of the Dead Lands coast, kept by grave-wives.

warden_vigil.spirit_desc: Mirolon honours the gods as watchers. Every warden keeps a night vigil each month, and every tower keeps its lamp toward the south.
warden_vigil.text: The watch-faith of Mirolon, led by vigil-captains.

hearth_iron.spirit_desc: A bar of iron is kept at every hearth and passed to the eldest son. Old feuds are settled over the bar.
hearth_iron.text: The iron-faith of Dondor, kept by smiths called iron-keepers.
